'''Gero Decher''' is a German chemist and Distinguished Professor ("Professeur classe exceptionnelle") at the Faculty of Chemistry of [[University of Strasbourg]]. He is best known for his seminal role in the development of [[polyelectrolyte]] multilayers, which is today known as “[[Layer by layer|layer-by-layer]] (LbL) assembly”,<ref>{{cite book|last=Decher|first=Gero|title=Multilayer thin films – sequential assembly of nanocomposite materials, vol 2.|year=2012|publisher=Wiley-VCH|location=Weinheim, Germany}}</ref> a simple yet powerful nanofabrication method that has enabled the development of entirely new technologies, such as [[Biocompatibility|biocompatible]] coatings on [[medical device]]s, ultrastrong [[nanocomposite]]s, [[Brain–computer interface|neural interfaces]], charge-storage devices, gas separation, fire retardants, and [[gene delivery]] platforms. According to CNRS International Magazine, Decher's work has “sparked a small revolution in materials science”.<ref name=CNRS>{{cite web|url = http://www.cnrs.fr/fr/pdf/cim/CIM29.pdf |title=CNRS International Magazine |publisher=CNRS |date=2013 |accessdate=8 October 2017}}</ref> [[Layer by layer|Layer-by-layer]] assembly is now an established part of the [[nanobiotechnology]] curriculum.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/Remodelled-Biotech-Curriculum_Animal-Biotechnology.pdf |title=Meeting Educational Needs with "Course" Correction – Remodelled M.Sc. Animal Biotechnology Curriculum |publisher=Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science & Technology, Government of India |date=2017 |accessdate=8 October 2017}}</ref>

Decher's work on the [[self-assembly]] and buildup of multilayer films by alternating application of [[Ion|anionic and cationic]] components during the early 1990s<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1002/masy.19910460145 | title = Buildup of ultrathin multilayer films by a self-assembly process, consecutive adsorption of anionic and cationic bipolar amphiphiles on charged surfaces | year = 1991 |author1=Gero Decher |author2=Jong-Dal Hong | journal = Macromolecular Symposia | volume = 46 | page = 321}}</ref> is generally credited for the revitalization of the [[Layer by layer|layer-by-layer]] assembly technique and its current prevalence in [[Nanotechnology|nanoscience]].<ref name=CNRS /> His 1997 article on “fuzzy nanoassemblies” published in [[Science (journal)|Science]] Magazine<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1126/science.277.5330.1232 | title = Fuzzy Nanoassemblies: Toward Layered Polymeric Multicomposites |url=http://www1.udel.edu/chem/polenova/PDF/Polyoxometalates/POM_layerPrep_Decher_Science1997.pdf| year = 1997 |author1=Gero Decher | journal = Science | volume = 277 | issue = 5330 | page = 1232}}</ref> highlighted the potential of [[Layer by layer|layer-by-layer]] assembly, and was identified by ISI as 8th most cited among all journal articles in chemistry in the decade 1997–2007. This article has been cited over 8000 times as of March 2019.

Over his career, Decher's research has focused on the [[Layer by layer|layer-by-layer]] assembly method, [[macromolecule]]s at interfaces, [[nanocomposite]] (bio)materials, (bio)functional [[nanoparticle]]s, functional coatings, [[Thin film|thin-film]] devices and nano-organized multi-materials in general. His current research is centered around the assembly of multi-[[nanocomposite]]s with complex [[Anisotropy|anisotropies]].

==Education and academic career==
Decher studied chemistry at [[University of Marburg|Philipps Universität]], in his hometown of [[Marburg]], [[Germany]]. Prior to completing his Diploma thesis with Gernot Boche on the [[Nuclear magnetic resonance|NMR spectroscopy]] of carbanions, he spent a year working with William Russey at [[Juniata College]] in [[Pennsylvania]]. In 1986 he obtained his PhD in [[organic chemistry]] from [[Johannes Gutenberg University of Mainz]], Germany, working in the laboratory of [[Helmut Ringsdorf]] on drug-carrying polymers and lyotropic liquid crystals. He then took up a position as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Novartis|Ciba-Geigy AG]] in [[Fribourg]], [[Switzerland]], where he worked with Bernd Tieke on non-centrosymmetric [[Langmuir-Blodgett film]]s. From 1988 to 1994 Decher was an Assistant Professor with Helmuth Möhwald at [[Johannes Gutenberg University of Mainz]], where he began his research on the development of [[Layer by layer|layer-by-layer]] assembly as part of his [[Habilitation]] in [[physical chemistry]]. From 1994 to 1995 he was Visiting Professor at [[University of Strasbourg|Université Louis Pasteur in Strasbourg]], France, and was promoted to Full Professor of Chemistry in 1995. His research laboratories are located at the [[Institut Charles Sadron|CNRS Institut Charles Sadron]] in [[Strasbourg]], [[France]], where he served as Deputy Director from 2001 to 2009. He was appointed Distinguished Professor by [[University of Strasbourg|Université Louis Pasteur]] (now Université de Strasbourg) in 2006.

==Professional achievements==
Decher is a member of the International Center for Frontier Research in Chemistry (ICFRC) and of the excellence cluster “Nanostructures and their Environment”, both in [[Strasbourg]]. He is also a Senior Member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] (IUF).<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.iufrance.fr/les-membres-de-liuf/membre/555-gero-decher.html |title=Les membres |publisher=Institut Universitaire de France |accessdate=8 October 2017}}</ref> Further distinctions awarded to Decher include the Emilia Valori Grand Prix of the [[Académie des sciences (France)]] for Nanobiotechnology in 2009,<ref name=valori /> the ECIS–Rhodia European Colloid & Interface Prize in 2010,<ref name=rhodia /> and the International Award of the [[Society of Polymer Science]] Japan in 2013. In 2015 he was selected as a participant for the [[Member of the European Parliament|Members of European Parliament]] Scientist Pairing Scheme, where he was teamed up with a member of the European Parliament.<ref name=pairing />
